title: INC-318 · Edge Capacity Breach
summary: A solved 110 Mbps split is mathematically unique, but one link exceeds its rated 60 Mbps capacity.
description: During the evening surge the gateway recorded a 110 Mbps total across three edge links plus two pairwise differences. The model is fully determined, and it reveals that link A is carrying 20 Mbps more than its documented capacity.
investigationSteps: Assign one variable to each monitored edge link.
Convert the total reading and both pairwise differences into equations.
Reduce the augmented matrix and confirm full column rank.
Compare every solved flow with the documented link capacity.
templateFindings: The three measurements are independent, so the model has full column rank and a unique answer.
RREF gives the split x₁ = 80, x₂ = 20 and x₃ = 10 Mbps.
Link A is rated for 60 Mbps but is carrying 80 Mbps, an overload of 20 Mbps.
suggestedActions: Move at least 20 Mbps from link A to a documented backup path.
Raise the link A capacity alert threshold and verify the rating in the asset register.
Re-run the model after the routing change and archive the new distribution.
